ordered_diagnoses: Germ cell tumor with somatic differentiation

s1.syndrome_frame: Painless scrotal swelling with testicular enlargement and solid masses
salient_findings: Large, solid masses in both testes on scrotal ultrasound
Tumor confined to the testis with lymphovascular invasion
key_facts: Scrotal ultrasound showed large, solid masses in both testes
Serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin, α-fetoprotein, and lactate dehydrogenase within normal limits
No evidence of lymphadenopathy or extranodal lymphomatous masses on PET-CT scan
Pleomorphic tumor composed of three distinct cell types: small cells, medium cells, and large cells

raw.rationale: The presence of a pleomorphic tumor composed of three distinct cell types and the lack of elevated serum tumor markers are consistent with a non-seminomatous germ cell tumor.

rejected.label: Seminoma
rejected.why: Seminomas are typically composed of uniform cells and often present with elevated serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin levels.

rejected.label: Embryonal carcinoma
rejected.why: While embryonal carcinomas can be pleomorphic, they often present with elevated serum α-fetoprotein levels, which were not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Teratoma
rejected.why: Teratomas are a type of non-seminomatous germ cell tumor, but the description of the tumor in this case does not specifically suggest the presence of teratomatous elements.

rejected.label: Germ cell tumor with somatic differentiation
rejected.why: While this diagnosis is possible, the information provided does not specifically suggest somatic differentiation, making non-seminomatous germ cell tumor a more general and appropriate diagnosis.
